headline: PLS.AX gets smacked 3.75% as lithium sentiment sours, while the ASX dipped and US tech slid last night despite a solid NASDAQ bounce.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara got hit hard today, dropping 3.75% to $5.91. Despite some optimistic headlines about a lithium 'surprise revival', the market isn't buying it yet — lithium spot prices remain under pressure and sentiment toward ASX lithium stocks is still cautious. PLS is now down 12.3% on your total investment.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slid 1.93% last night to $210.25, continuing its soft run. There's no specific catalyst in today's news — this looks like broader NASDAQ weakness dragging it down. Still sitting 9.3% below your average cost.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: The AI ETF fell 1.74% today to $18.05, which is a bit ironic given all the AI buzz in the news. The dip likely reflects the ASX 200 pulling back broadly today. Down 5.15% on your total investment.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google slipped 1.05% last night to $361.91. No specific news catalyst — it moved with the general tech pullback. Still up a healthy 25.2% on your total investment, so this is just a small wobble on a solid position.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Emerging markets edged down 0.94% today to $92.03. The Aussie dollar also fell against the USD today (down 1.07%), which can weigh on AUD-denominated emerging market funds. Small position, small loss.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft dipped 0.97% last night to $412.63. Like Google, no specific news drove this — just a quiet pullback across US tech names. Still sitting 6.88% below your buy-in price, so patience is the play here.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL slipped a modest 0.8% today to $8.70. Oil itself actually ticked up last night (WTI crude above $91), so this is a slight disconnect — likely just ASX-wide selling pressure dragging it down. Still up 2.86% overall.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS nudged up 0.31% today to $521.82, which is a decent result on a day the ASX slid broadly. The US total market ETF benefited from last night's strong NASDAQ session flowing through to today's ASX pricing. Up 1.19% on your investment.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG barely moved today, up a tiny 0.12% to $75.95. It's a diversified fund so it absorbs the good and bad across markets — a quiet day is a fine day. Up 0.76% overall, doing its job as a stable core holding.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Sharp 3.75% drop today — hold or trim?
watch_today.detail: Pilbara fell hard to $5.91 today and is now down 12.3% on your investment. There's talk of a lithium 'surprise revival' but the price action doesn't back that up yet. If you believe in the long-term EV battery demand story, hold tight — but this one needs watching closely. Don't add until there's a genuine price floor.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: AI ETF dips 1.74% despite positive AI headlines
watch_today.detail: The Global X AI ETF dropped 1.74% today to $18.05 and is 5.15% underwater. Ironically, the AI sector news is fairly constructive — OpenAI launched new security features and the EU is softening its AI regulation pace. The dip looks like general market weakness rather than an AI-specific problem. Hold and watch for a bounce.

watch_today.title: TTWO: Weakest mover in your US portfolio — hold for now
watch_today.detail: Take-Two fell 1.93% last night to $210.25 and is down 9.3% on your total investment. No specific news today — just drifting lower with the market. GTA VI is the big catalyst everyone's waiting for; without a release date update or earnings surprise, there's not much to act on. Hold and be patient.

watch_today.title: AUD fell 1.07% today — good for your US holdings
watch_today.detail: The Australian dollar dropped to US$0.7056 today. This is actually a quiet tailwind for your US-denominated holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) — when the AUD is weaker, your US investments are worth more in Aussie dollar terms. Keeps an eye on this if the RBA signals a rate pause this week.

watch_today.title: RBA rate decision watch — pause expected
watch_today.detail: Multiple reports today suggest the RBA is expected to pause on interest rate hikes at its next meeting, as inflation risks persist but the economy is showing stress. A pause would be good news for growth stocks (including your tech ETFs and GXAI.AX) and could put upward pressure on the AUD. Watch for the RBA decision and any statement language carefully.

watch_today.title: Anthropic eyes Australia — big electricity demand incoming
watch_today.detail: AI company Anthropic (maker of Claude) is reportedly planning a major data centre push in Australia that could consume a large slice of the country's electricity output. This is a big structural signal for Australian energy infrastructure and could be a longer-term tailwind for energy-exposed holdings like FUEL.AX. Green flag for the broader AI and energy theme.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 slipped 0.7% today to close at 8,625 — a soft session with broad selling across the board. Last night in the US, it was a different story: the NASDAQ jumped 1.27% and the S&P 500 gained 0.66%, suggesting US tech found its footing after recent weakness. Oil ticked up slightly to $91.14 a barrel, gold hit $4,364 an ounce (continuing its strong run), and the Aussie dollar fell 1.07% to US$0.7056 — meaning each US dollar now costs you more Aussie cents.

politics.summary: The RBA is dominating local headlines today, with debate about whether it will pause rate hikes at its next meeting. Meanwhile, Anthropic's plans to plant a massive AI data centre in Australia are raising energy grid questions.

stories.title: RBA tipped to pause as inflation risks persist
stories.why_it_matters: Markets are now leaning towards the RBA holding interest rates steady at its next meeting rather than hiking again. Inflation remains a concern but signs of economic strain are making the central bank cautious. A pause would be welcome relief for mortgage holders and could give growth-oriented stocks — including the tech ETFs in your portfolio — a bit of a lift. Watch for the official decision and the language in the RBA's statement.

stories.title: RBA defends rate hikes: 'Other countries would kill for our problems'
stories.why_it_matters: The RBA is defending its aggressive rate hike campaign, with officials pointing out that Australia's unemployment rate and economic growth are still relatively strong compared to other countries. The 'our problems are good problems' framing suggests the RBA isn't panicking — but it also isn't promising cuts anytime soon. Property investors and borrowers shouldn't expect rates to fall quickly.

stories.title: Anthropic has its eyes on Australia — and a large slice of its electricity output
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic, the US AI company behind the Claude chatbot, is reportedly planning a significant data centre presence in Australia. The scale is apparently large enough that it could meaningfully impact national electricity demand. This signals big investment in Australian AI infrastructure but also raises questions about grid capacity and energy pricing — a potential tailwind for energy stocks and utilities over the medium term.

ai.summary: AI regulation is the big theme today — OpenAI launched a new security feature, the EU is softening its regulatory timeline, and Anthropic is making a major Australian power play. Lots of moving parts for the industry.

stories.title: OpenAI Launches Lockdown Mode To Block Prompt Injection Attacks
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI has rolled out a new 'Lockdown Mode' for its AI systems, designed to block 'prompt injection attacks' — that's when someone tries to trick an AI by hiding malicious instructions inside innocent-looking text (like embedding commands in a webpage the AI is asked to read). This is a real and growing security problem as AI gets used in business workflows. It shows OpenAI is taking enterprise security seriously, which matters for MSFT (which distributes OpenAI tools via Copilot) and GOOG (which faces the same threats with Gemini).

stories.title: EU Delays Key AI Rules as Brussels Reconsiders Pace of Regulation
stories.why_it_matters: The European Union is pumping the brakes on some of its AI rulebook, delaying key parts of the EU AI Act as regulators reconsider how fast they're moving. Brussels is worried about stifling innovation and falling behind the US and China. For companies like Google and Microsoft selling AI products into Europe, this is a small win — fewer rules in the short term means less compliance cost and faster deployment of new features.

stories.title: Anthropic has its eyes on Australia — and a large slice of its electricity output
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic — the AI startup founded by ex-OpenAI researchers and backed by Google — is planning a major Australian data centre expansion that would consume a significant portion of Australia's electricity grid. This is a massive vote of confidence in Australia as an AI hub, but it also signals how energy-hungry these AI systems are becoming. Longer term, it's a structural tailwind for Australian energy infrastructure and could benefit energy-exposed ETFs like FUEL.AX.

stories.title: EU AI Act Update: European Commission Publishes Draft Guidelines on High-Risk AI
stories.why_it_matters: Even while delaying some rules, the EU has published draft guidelines for 'high-risk AI' — systems used in things like hiring, credit scoring, medical devices, and critical infrastructure. Companies deploying AI in these areas will face strict transparency and accountability requirements. This adds compliance complexity for big tech players but also creates an opening for AI governance and security tools — a theme your GXAI.AX ETF is exposed to.

sport.summary: NRL Round 14 wrapped up with some big scorelines — the Tigers copped a 68-point belting and the Panthers kept rolling. AFL had a tight Dees win plus an AFL rule controversy and the first Big Freeze since Neale Daniher's passing. Round 15 NRL kicks off Thursday night.

stories.title: 'Done nothing with him': Tigers cop 68-point disaster as Blues sweat on Panthers blow
stories.why_it_matters: Wests Tigers were absolutely demolished in Round 14 — a 68-point loss that has critics calling out the coaching staff for how they're handling their roster. The Panthers won comfortably again and are streaking away at the top of the table, though NSW Blues selectors are apparently sweating on the fitness of at least one Panthers player ahead of State of Origin. Tigers fans should probably look away.

stories.title: NRL Roundup: Panthers skip away as an interesting logjam forms
stories.why_it_matters: Penrith Panthers are pulling clear at the top of the NRL ladder after another strong Round 14 result. Below them, a tight logjam is forming in the top 8 with multiple teams separated by just a few competition points. With the Dolphins hosting the Roosters at Suncorp on Friday night in Round 15, there's plenty of pressure footy coming up for Gold Coast viewers.

stories.title: BLOG RECAP: Dees win thriller, Mihocek taken to hospital, Pies star out
stories.why_it_matters: Melbourne Demons won a tense AFL thriller over the weekend, but it came at a cost — Collingwood's Nick Mihocek was taken to hospital during the game (details on his condition are still emerging) and a Pies star has been ruled out going forward. The Dees needed the win to stay in touch with the top four. Drama all round for Collingwood fans.

stories.title: Celebrities slip and slide in first Big Freeze event since Neale Daniher's death
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL's iconic Big Freeze fundraiser returned to the MCG today — the first one since the death of Neale Daniher, the former Melbourne coach who inspired the event to raise money for MND (Motor Neurone Disease) research. Celebrities took the famous slide into a pool of ice at halftime of the Queen's Birthday clash. An emotional and important day for the footy community.

stories.title: AFL world calls for immediate rule change after 'loophole' helps Carlton beat Essendon
stories.why_it_matters: Carlton beat Essendon using what commentators and fans are calling a rules 'loophole', sparking immediate calls for the AFL to change the rule. The AFL world is pretty fired up about it — when a team wins via a technicality rather than football skill, it tends to get everyone talking. The AFL may be forced to address this at its next rules committee meeting.
